request.title: Gate worker spawns and merges on the harness store
request.expect:
Machine first: the first commit changes `spec/*.machine.json` (plus failing tests) so the workItem machine records each worker spawn (role builder, verifier or triager; the agent actor from #33; sha256 of the brief; agent type; model; harness version) and refuses a builder spawn until a verifier brief hash is fixed for the item, and refuses a verifier spawn whose brief hash differs from the fixed one. SPEC.md is re-rendered and shows these guards; no new refusal lives only in host code.
Standing, versioned agent definitions `plugins/harness/agents/builder.md` and `verifier.md` carry the rules that must not drift per brief: machines first (a rule is a guard in the JSON, not a host check), concepts added, merged or removed instead of growth, build only what the item needs, keep SPEC.md and the README true, and for the verifier the distrust, blind and hard-limit rules of the Verifier section below. Builder and verifier spawns use these agent types, and the spawn record names the definition's version.
An agent actor is believed only when the plugin's own PreToolUse record says that agent ran the command: the hook records (session, agent_id, tool_use_id or command hash, time) for every Bash call that runs `harness`, and the CLI refuses an event whose claimed agent does not match the record for the call it is running in, so an obfuscated `HARNESS_AGENT` (for example `env "HARNESS_""AGENT=<other>:builder" harness …`, found by #33's verifier) records nothing. A `harness` call the hook did not see records nothing under `HARNESS_ENFORCE=1`.
Spawn gate: a plugin PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool, on when `HARNESS_ENFORCE=1`, denies (with a reason naming the rule) a spawn that names an item role unless the item is triaged in the store and the machine would take the spawn; on an allowed spawn it records the spawn event in the store, and SubagentStart binds the new agent_id to it. A spawn with no item role is allowed but its agent can send no item event (run result, criterion check, triage) for any item.
Merge gate: a plugin PreToolUse hook, on when `HARNESS_ENFORCE=1`, on `mcp__github__merge_pull_request`, `gh pr merge`, and `gh api` calls to a pull's merge endpoint, denies the merge unless the PR is bound to an item whose machine would take `MERGED` now the store holds the item's verifier verdict PASS for the exact head sha being merged, and the PR carries that verdict as a review on that sha (`commit_id`). The merge call must pin the head sha (`expectedHeadSha`, `--match-head-commit` or `sha`).
The verifier's verbatim verdict is on the PR as a review with event COMMENT on the head sha it checked, ending with the brief's sha256, and the same verdict is an event in the store from the verifier's agent actor. The CLI gives the verifier one command that does both from a verdict file. (A `harness/verifier` commit status cannot be set: the session proxy refuses POST statuses with 403, measured 2026-10-27.)
With `HARNESS_ENFORCE` unset, both hooks only record and never deny. Like the other hooks they are silent no-ops in a project without the install marker, and exit 0 on their own failure; under `HARNESS_ENFORCE=1` a gate that cannot reach the store denies instead of allowing.
`harness doctor` lists, as a problem, every merged PR bound to an item that has no verifier PASS in the store for its merge head, or no PASS review on GitHub on that sha.
End to end, in a headless `claude -p --plugin-dir <worktree>/plugins/harness` run with `HARNESS_ENFORCE=1` and a scratch store: a builder spawn before the verifier brief is fixed is denied; after fixing it, the builder spawn is allowed and recorded with its agent_id; a merge call without the status is denied. Commands and outputs are in the PR body.
No refusal lives only in host code: a CI check fails when a `refused:` path in `packages/harness/src` or a deny in the plugin hooks has no guard or named host invariant in the spec. The PR body lists the concepts (CLI commands, events, files, hooks) it adds, merges and removes.
`npm test` passes with and without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; CI is green; the plugin bundle check passes.

request.title: Put every harness refusal in the spec, enforced by one runtime path
request.expect:
Every event refusal the harness makes is a guard in `spec/*.machine.json` (the harness machine holds the PR-to-item map as an event with a guard, for example `PR_BOUND` / `prNotBound`), or, where XState cannot express it, a named host invariant listed in SPEC.md under "Host invariants"; SPEC.md is re-rendered and a reader learns every refusal from it.
The runtime enforces them through one generic path; the rule-specific host functions this replaces are removed.
Behaviour is unchanged: the existing binding, branch and refusal tests pass unmodified in what they assert (a test may move, not weaken).
The PR body lists concepts (CLI commands, events, guards, files, functions) added, merged and removed, and host lines in `packages/harness/src`, `bin` and `plugins/harness/scripts` go down.
`npm test` passes with and without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; CI is green.

request.title: Harness pages ship in the plugin and are current when viewed
Let the person grant the stand-in what it may decide for them
request.expect:
Machine first: the spec defines a grant the person gives the stand-in (which decision kinds it may decide alone, and until when), recorded only from the person's tap on a checklist card the machine asked for, like PERSON_DECIDED; SPEC.md shows it. Nothing else can create, widen or extend a grant.
Every decision says whether it is a two-way door (cheaply reversible) or a one-way door; the stand-in decides alone only on a two-way door whose kind the live grant covers, or on a one-way door the grant names explicitly. Outside the grant, the ladder rule applies as today.
A grant ends at its end time or when the person taps a new checklist; an expired or replaced grant decides nothing.
The checklist card's options are generated by the machine (decision kinds, the one-way-door box, the end time), and the person's ticks arrive as one tap event naming the card.
Every decision the stand-in made under a grant is listed for the person (mission control and the daily audit) with its reason, so the person can reverse it.
The PR body lists concepts added, merged and removed; host code grows only where an Expect line needs it.
`npm test` passes with and without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; CI is green.

criteria: Opening mission control or the ledger page shows the store and ledgers as they are now, or plainly shows how old the data is and offers a button that brings it up to date.
No refresh happens without a viewer. An idle project spends nothing on pages.
Every refresh records its duration, the store version or ledger size it rendered, and when it ran. The page shows the trend.
`harness doctor` flags a refresh slower than a set threshold.

The guided tour is part of the plugin. Its content about states, events and guards comes from the current `spec/*.machine.json` and SPEC.md. Hand-written parts name the spec version they were written for, or CI checks them against the spec.
Each page declares its data needs and spec references in one file in the repo (for example `pages/<page>/needs.json`) and reads nothing else.

`npm test` fails, naming the page and the missing piece, when a runtime, store or spec change breaks any page's declared needs. The test builds its store with the current runtime (the sim), not a frozen fixture.
A test fails when the spec has a state, event or guard that the tour does not cover.
A page opened on a store whose `schemaVersion` is outside its declared range shows a red banner naming the mismatch, and never shows partial data as complete.
A fresh install from the plugin alone (no Library, no memory) gets all three pages working against `harness/state/<store>` (the dogfood store here, never `main`).

answer.reason: Revise, not cancel: the independent verifier FAILed two Expect lines that the issue makes hard limits (partial breach = FAIL). (1) BLOCK and CANCEL from a no-role agent, or from a builder on an item it has no spawn on, are accepted by the store, so 'no item event' is not met. (2) The merge gate misses gh pr merge inside { }, if/for/while, '!', functions, bash -c, setsid/stdbuf/find -exec and 'gh pr --repo o/r merge', so the gate does not read every command (SPEC readableGitHubWrite). The other 14 lines are met and the design is sound, so send it back to the builder to fix these two, rather than cancel it. Do not accept it, because the gaps are exactly the unaudited-merge hole this item exists to close.
